layout.title: How Car Brakes Work

shows.does: a wooden block slides down onto the spinning tire, sparks fly where it touches
dark smoke pours off the tire where the block rubs
the block lifts off, a steel disc appears on the hub and a red caliper grips it
the pads touch the disc lightly and it keeps spinning
a pedal, a master cylinder and a pipe to the caliper appear, orange fluid runs down it
a glowing outline traces the caliper on the disc
the pedal goes down, the pads clamp hard and the disc glows red hot
vents open in the disc, white air arrows blow through and the glow fades
the pads grab and the wheel stops dead in a flash: it locks
the wheel turns again and the pads pulse on and off against the disc
the pulsing pads stop the wheel, and nothing on the stand warns anyone behind
a red brake light appears on a post beside the pedal
the tire spins, the pedal swings down, the light glows and the wheel stops

layout.why: A cut-open disc brake on a stand in a home workshop: a block presses the spinning tire, then a disc and caliper, a pedal with its fluid pipe, vents, anti-lock pulsing and a brake light are added one by one, following the push from the tire to the pedal fluid to the road and the car behind. Close shots on the tire and disc for each change, wider ones when the pedal joins.

sentences.text: If you press a block on a spinning tire, you have a brake.
But the rubber grinds and smokes.
So you bolt on a disc and squeeze it.
But your squeeze is weak; the disc spins on.
So you add a pedal that pushes fluid.
But the fluid clamps hard, and the disc glows red.
So you cut vents, and air cools it.
But on wet roads, the cooled wheel locks up.
So you add anti-lock brakes that pulse the pads.
But the pulsing pads stop you, unseen from behind.
So you add a brake light.
Press the pedal, and the spinning tire stops.
Congratulations, you built a disc brake.

recurring.what: the tire with its white mark: spinning, smoking, locking, and stopping at the end

chain.shows: smoke pours off the tire under the block
the weak squeeze barely touches the disc and it keeps spinning
the fluid clamps the pads and the disc glows red hot
the cooled wheel stops dead and locks
chain.stakes: the car skids and cannot steer

chain.shows: the pulsing pads stop the wheel with no warning
chain.stakes: the car behind runs into you

ideas.idea: pressing a block on a spinning tire is the simplest brake
the rubber grinds against the block and smokes
a steel disc on the hub is squeezed instead of the tire
a hand squeeze is too weak to stop the disc
a pedal pushes fluid down a pipe to the caliper, multiplying the push
the disc and its caliper are a disc brake
the fluid clamps so hard the disc heats up and glows
vents let air through the disc to cool it
on a wet road the wheel locks instead of slowing
anti-lock brakes pulse the pads on and off so the wheel keeps turning
the car stops hard and the driver behind gets no warning
a brake light comes on with the pedal
press the pedal and the spinning tire stops, the light glows
